issues.claim: Kafka: партиции, журнал только с дозаписью, retention, log compaction, offset у каждой группы потребителей, порядок внутри партиции, параллелизм группы ограничен числом партиций
issues.problem: The excerpt of https://kafka.apache.org/intro shows only that Kafka stores event streams durably 'for as long as you want' and describes clients and events. It does not show partitions, log compaction, per-group offsets, ordering within a partition or the cap on group parallelism. The rebuttal says a full-page refetch is needed and does not supply that evidence. The intro page is also unlikely to cover compaction or consumer-group assignment at all.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or replace with a documentation page whose fetched excerpt shows these claims (the Design or Consumer sections of the versioned Kafka docs, for example https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#design). Refetch it, confirm the excerpt, and add a matching linkTitles entry in both locales.

issues.claim: RabbitMQ Streams сокращают этот разрыв: журнал только с дозаписью, чтение не удаляет сообщения, потребитель может начать с выбранного смещения
issues.problem: The excerpt starts mid-page and covers replication, data safety, resource use and offset tracking. It never states that a stream is an append-only log that is read non-destructively from a chosen offset. The rebuttal only asserts that the opening section says this. That is an assertion, not evidence from an excerpt.
issues.suggestedFix: Refetch the page and confirm the opening section ('What are Streams') shows the append-only, non-destructive, read-from-any-offset wording. If it does not, cite a stream-specific page (for example the RabbitMQ stream overview or stream plugin guide) that does.

issues.claim: RabbitMQ: exchange, bindings, типы exchange (direct, topic, fanout, headers), подтверждение каждого сообщения, удаление после подтверждения
issues.problem: The excerpt of the AMQP 0-9-1 page covers methods, connections, channels, vhosts and extensibility. It shows nothing about exchanges, bindings, exchange types or acknowledgements. The page itself very likely covers them, but the excerpt does not support the specific claims.
issues.suggestedFix: Refetch the page and confirm the exchange/binding/ack sections appear in the excerpt. If they do not, add a source that shows them (for example https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/confirms for acknowledgements).

issues.claim: Документация Kafka ... говорит, что exactly-once для внешних систем-получателей обычно требует их участия, а Kafka лишь даёт смещение, с помощью которого это можно реализовать.
issues.problem: The fetched page is still a 'Redirecting...' stub, so the excerpt shows none of this wording. It also shows none of the idempotent-producer, read_committed or Kafka Streams claims. The rebuttal quotes the sentence from memory and offers no excerpt, so it is a bare assertion. The explanation names the Message Delivery Semantics section as the source, so this claim is directly checkable and currently unchecked.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a URL whose fetch returns the real text, for example https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#semantics or a versioned URL such as https://kafka.apache.org/41/documentation/#semantics. Refetch it and confirm the excerpt contains the 'cooperation with such systems ... offset' sentence. Otherwise remove the attribution to the documentation and rely on KIP-98 and the microservices.io page.

issues.problem: The URL works but redirected to a different canonical page. The excerpt supports atomic writes to topic partitions plus offset commits via sendOffsetsToTransaction. It does not explicitly state that external systems are out of scope, so the phrase 'likewise scopes them' is an inference.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the canonical URL https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/KAFKA/pages/66854913/KIP-98+-+Exactly+Once+Delivery+and+Transactional+Messaging. Soften the wording to: 'KIP-98, which designed transactions, describes them as atomic writes across Kafka partitions together with consumer offset commits.'
